_README: Per-income-year IRS deduction rules, one self-contained rule set per year, for the past-year re-audit. A re-audit of year N MUST use year N's rules. Proven necessary: art. 78.º-E (rendas) changed in force in 2024, 2025 AND 2026, and is not a single ceiling but an escalonamento (15% base + majoracoes 50%/75%). Using today's value for a past year ships wrong numbers - the same green-but-wrong class as the Excel-serial and page-count bugs.
_structure: years.<income_year>.rules.<key> holds {pct, ceiling, ...params, verified, source_law}. One year is authoritative only when every rule in it is verified=true. Downstream docs (deducoes.html, cae_sectors.json, Bible ch.15) should READ the current year from here instead of hardcoding their own copy - today they each carry a separate copy with no cross-check.
_provenance: Values come from each article's DEDICATED DRE page (2014-70048167-<id>), which exposes the in-force text + full 'Alteracoes ao artigo' history; the full consolidated render does NOT expose those accordions. Historical (past-year) text is read by viewing the article as-in-force at that year. source_law names the diploma that set the value for that year.
_correction_windows: How long each past year stays fixable is separate, in legal_sources.json: cppt-59 (substituicao), cppt-70 (reclamacao graciosa 120 dias), lgt-78 (revisao 4 anos, com limites).
_status: COMPLETE for 2023/2024/2025 (2026-07-24): all 6 base ceilings + global limit + dependentes + 78-E sub-limits, verified via portaldasfinancas (cirs_pf.py) with redacao-law provenance. DRE = source of record. Refinements possible: exact escalao thresholds (track art 68/68-A brackets yearly), 78-E rendas escalonamento formula.
_method_proven: Historical (past-year) values come from the OE law's own consolidated ARTICLE page (small, ~13k chars, clean via dre.mjs get), NOT the SPA version-at-date control and NOT the 200-page OE PDF. Workflow, deterministic: (1) the CIRS article's amendment history names the amending law+article, e.g. '78.º-E <- Lei 82/2023, art. 230'; (2) search 'OE <year> Artigo <N>' for that page's id (ids are non-sequential OutSystems content ids, not guessable, but search finds them); (3) dre.mjs get that page; (4) parse the redacao block '«Artigo N ...»' - the format is legally standardized across every OE, so the parser generalizes. PROVEN 2026-07-23: OE-2024 art 230 (2023-836109751-836144477) yields 78.º-E 2024 base rendas limit = 600 EUR (n.4 adds escalonamento: 900 EUR for rendimento coletavel <= 1st escalao). Current single-article isolation from the full consolidated render also works via the fixed line-anchored matcher (no re-render needed).
_rule_latest_amendment_per_year: For income year Y, an article's value = the redacao set by the LAST amendment IN FORCE for Y, not the first. 78.º-E was amended TWICE for 2024 (Lei 82/2023 -> 600, then Lei 36/2024 in force 2024-08-07). 600 is the Lei 82/2023 wording and MUST be reconciled with Lei 36/2024 before verified=true.

current_values_2026_verified_isolation._note: Extracted from the CIRS consolidated PDF via node pdf-parse v2 (PDFParse class) - the SPA innerText collapses nested list items, the PDF does not. Method now proven; earlier 'PDF not needed' note was WRONG.
current_values_2026_verified_isolation.78.º-E: escalonamento; 296/450 sao os JUROS sub-cases; rendas base per year (2024=600 via OE-2024)
current_values_2026_verified_isolation.78.º_n7_global_limit: sem limite abaixo do 1.o escalao (~7703); formula entre ~7703 e 80000; teto 1000 acima de 80000; n.8 majoracao 3+ dependentes. NOTA: PDF glitchou o limiar inferior ('a.000') - confirmar 7703.

amendment_map._note: Years an amendment came INTO FORCE, from the dedicated pages. A rule is STABLE for target years if nothing came into force within them; then all target years = current value (verified by absence of change). A rule that changed within 2023-2025 needs the as-in-force text read per year.
